title: Cross-functional deployment nudge framework - sketch
content:
Purpose:
This is a working sketch for a 'nudge' driven rollout pattern intended to sit between micro-canaries and full cohort AB experiments. The idea: instead of static step jumps (0->1%->5%->25%), use short, observable nudges that adapt based on fast signals and human guardrails.

Intended audience:
- Product owners coordinating cross-team releases
- Console/ops engineers implementing exposure controls
- Oncall and SREs responsible for safety thresholds
- Solutions & SEs running customer pilots

High-level goals:
- Reduce oscillation risk when model behaviour is brittle by ramping exposure in many small nudges rather than large jumps.
- Surface early soft signals (semantic drift, hallucination spikes) quickly with short windows so humans can react.
- Keep cost predictable via nudge-size-aware batching and autoscale policies.
- Provide a readable, enforceable contract for downstream stakeholders (support, legal, sales) about exposure cadence and revert conditions.

Definitions / lexicon (for this doc):
- Nudge: a short-duration, small-volume exposure increment (e.g., add 0.25% traffic for 10–30m).
- Nudge window: duration during which signals are evaluated for that nudge.
- Annealing: gradual increase in nudge size over a series of nudges to reach a target exposure.
- Pulse test: a synthetic traffic injection used to sanity-check observability and fallback.

When to use nudges instead of classic canaries:
- High-latency or expensive model variants where cost of rollback is high.
- Customer-facing features with high reputational risk (billing flows, policy decisions).
- Interdependent feature surfaces where one bad output can cascade (chained LLM calls).

Components of the framework:
1) Nudge Scheduler (console-level):
   - orchestrates timed nudges, supports randomized jitter to prevent correlated bursts across regions.
   - parameters: base_nudge_pct, nudge_increment_pct, nudge_duration_mins, jitter_pct, max_concurrent_nudges.

2) Fast Signal Engine (observability hooks):
   - 1-min / 5-min metric windows for error-rate, hallucination score (model eval proxy), latency p95/p99, token-cost delta, user complaint rate.
   - mechanism to mark a signal as ‘soft’ vs ‘hard’ (soft: needs human review; hard: auto-block).

3) Safety Contract (experiment metadata):
   - owner, stakeholders, business impact, revert owner, phone/Slack roster, backout procedure link.
   - encoded thresholds for auto-block (e.g., p99 latency +50% baseline and absolute p99 > 2s).

4) Pulse and Synthetic Traffic harness:
   - quick synthetic probes that exercise the same model paths as real traffic. Used immediately before a nudge.

5) Human-in-loop escalation runbook:
   - 3-step path: observe -> triage (ops + model) -> decide (revert / hold / continue).
   - accountability: who rubber-stamps >5% exposure increments.

Nudge policy heuristics (starter rules to iterate on):
- Base_nudge_pct = 0.25% for public web traffic; 0.5% for authenticated internal users.
- Nudge_duration = 20m by default (min 10m, max 60m).
- If any hard signal fires during the window -> immediate auto-block + reduce exposure to previous stable slice.
- If 2+ soft signals exceed soft thresholds in one nudge window -> hold and require human approval.
- Annealing schedule example: 0.25% -> 0.5% -> 1% -> (pause, longer window) -> 2.5% -> 5% -> 10% -> 25%
- Randomized jitter: each nudge start time jitter +/- 10% to avoid synchronized spikes across regions.

Metrics & evaluation windows (practical notes):
- Use rolling median + IQR for noisy signals (avoid chasing outliers).
- Evaluate both delta relative to baseline and rolling absolute value (e.g., hallucination_rate delta > 0.4% AND absolute > 0.8% triggers soft).
- Latency: track both p95 relative and server-side processing tokens/sec.
- Cost: token consumption / session and projected monthly delta at current nudge sizes (important for Finance).

Observability wiring checklist (ops TODOs):
- [ ] 1-min ingestion for critical signals (errors, p95, hallucination proxy).
- [ ] Pulse harness endpoint + synthetic user scripts stored in infra repo.
- [ ] Dashboard tile: nudge timeline with annotations, current active nudge ID and owner.
- [ ] Automated slack ops-notify with short summary + links to trace IDs.

Human ceremony & stakeholder comms (practical pattern):
- Pre-nudge: 30m notice to core-stakeholders (ops, product, ML) for >1% total exposure change.
- During rollouts: skinny standup every 60m while exposure < 5%; switch to async updates thereafter.
- Post rollouts: 1-day postmortem if any hard signal fired or customer-impacting behaviour seen.

Simulation approach (how to test this before live traffic):
- Run 100 simulated nudges against a staging model with noise injection to validate false-positive rate of detectors.
- Include interleaved load tests at expected concurrency to observe autoscale and queuing behaviour.
- Turn on ‘dry-run’ mode in scheduler to let team experience notifications without changing traffic.

Example scenario (concrete numbers):
- Target: migrate reranker model from v1 -> v2 for logged-in users.
- Baseline p99 = 700ms; baseline hallucination proxy = 0.6%; baseline support rate = 0.02%.
- Nudge plan: 0.25% for 20m (pulse + monitor), then 0.5% for 20m, 1% for 30m, pause 2h, then 2.5%->5%->10% (longer windows).
- Auto-block conditions: p99 > 1.5s OR hallucination_proxy_delta > 0.8% absolute OR support_rate > 0.5% over nudge window.
- If auto-block occurs: scheduler immediately reverts traffic and opens a ticket to PRJ-4521 (example).

Rollout contract template (to be stored as metadata alongside experiment):
- Title, owner, business-impact, exposure-limit, auto-block thresholds, revert-owner, oncall roster, expected cost delta, legal/privacy notes, customers to exclude.

Edge cases and unresolved questions (notes-to-self):
- How to handle dependent multi-step LLM chains where upstream nudges cause noisy downstream signals? (option: couple nudges across components or use isolation slices).
- Should we allow overlapping nudges for different experiments if they affect disjoint user cohorts? risk: combinatorial interactions.
- How to standardize hallucination proxy? multiple teams are still experimenting with metrics (semantic-similarity vs classifier). We need a canonical lightweight signal for fast blocking.
- Coordination with Partner Integrations (dedicated / private deployments) — need a variant of the scheduler that emits an API token / signed intent to on-prem controllers.

Quick action items (next 2 weeks):
- Diego: prototype a scheduler endpoint that supports jitter and dry-run (branch: infra/rollout-sim#987).
- Priya: draft a canonical hallucination proxy spec and test harness.
- Lucas: stub observability dashboard tiles and slack summarizer (alerts channel: #rollout-nudges).
- Aisha: draft rollout contract metadata template and embed in Console create-flow.

Reference links and artifacts:
- confluence:CFG-1289-nudge-framework (design doc, WIP)
- JIRA PRJ-4521 (migration epic)
- github infra/rollout-sim#987 (scheduler prototype)

Loose thoughts / scribbles:
- Could we treat nudges as first-class objects in the console with a small DSL: nudge {pct:0.25, dur:20m, pulse:true, signals:[latency,pct_err,hall]}
- Consider a ‘safety escrow’ account (internal only) that gets full traffic fallback in case a customer-impacting revert is required rapidly.

If you're reading this and want to help: pick a TODO above, add notes inline, and ping me in #rollout-nudges.

---
End of sketch. This is intentionally rough; we want feedback on the sample thresholds and the ceremony cadence before we standardize across Console.
